messages:
Maya: seeing a spike of SIGTERM events on controller-manager and apiserver connection resets in eu-west1, started ~5m ago. pods are flapping on control-plane nodes. anyone else?
Jordan: yep, alerted. etcd leader changed 3x in the last 2m. controller-manager restarted twice. logs show 'context canceled' right before kubeclient calls fail.
Li: interesting — we had a burst of GPU node scale-outs in the same region ~6m ago for a training job. autoscaler may have induced pod migrations? :thinking:
ops-bot: [incident] control-plane-flap recorded for cluster: prod-eu-west1 at 2027-08-05T12:33:09Z
Maya: attaching top errors from apiserver logs: 
```
E0831 12:33:12.123456 1 request.go:123] apiserver panic: unexpected EOF
W0831 12:33:12.124000 1 trace.go:205] Trace[345]: "Get /api/v1/namespaces/default/pods" (started: 2027-08-05 12:33:11.999) (total time: 89ms)
```
Jordan: kubelet logs on cp-node-3 show frequent SIGTERM for kube-apiserver container, but systemd reports OOM? Not consistent.
Li: I pulled etcd metrics — election_latency spiked and follower replication lag increased. Looks like transient network packet drops between cp nodes around 12:32:50.
Maya: could the autoscaler + new GPU NICs have pushed more overlay traffic to the control-plane subnet? We changed CNI kernel modules in the 12:20 deploy.
Jordan: good call — the 12:18 kernel module rollout touched eni offload flags. If offload is inconsistent we could see partial packet loss + long RTTs causing etcd timeouts -> elections.
SRE Oncall: action plan: 1) cordon new GPU worker nodes added at 12:20 2) pin controller-manager replicas to remaining healthy cp nodes 3) throttle autoscaler 4) restart kubelet on cp-node-3 if OOM persists.
Li: executing step 1 now: `kubectl cordon gpu-worker-42` — cordon succeeded.
Maya: temporarily set autoscaler policy to zero-scale-burst via ops API (reduces rapid add/remove).
Jordan: redeploying controller-manager with env KUBE_CLIENT_TIMEOUT=30s to tolerate transient latency while we investigate.
Maya: also toggled netpolicy enforcement to permissive in eu-west1 since policies traverse iptables chains that were getting long after new nodes.
ops-bot: [deploy] controller-manager rollout started by Jordan.
Li: after cordoning the recent workers, etcd stabilization started. leader changed once, then held for 90s. replication lag down to baseline.
Maya: will keep monitoring for 10m. if stable, we'll revert netpolicy and autoscaler changes carefully.
Jordan: note for postmortem: interaction between GPU node scale bursts, CNI kernel offload changes, and control-plane network saturation. also check kube-system memory headroom on cp nodes — we had low mem margin on cp-node-3.
SRE Oncall: assigning postmortem to @Maya and @Jordan. tagging incident severity: Sev2.
Maya: thanks — I'll capture timelines and metrics. quick mitigation checklist saved: cordon, throttle autoscaler, restart kubelet, tolerate env flag, netpol permissive.
Li: graph links: https://grafana.internal/r/abcd (etcd elections), https://grafana.internal/r/efgh (apiserver latencies).
Jordan: FYI costs: throttling autoscaler might increase short-term cost because we pinned some GPU nodes for stability, but avoids broader outage. ops will reconcile.
Maya: update: 8m after the change apiserver connections look stable, no more SIGTERM spikes. leaving thread open until 12:53.
